name: Light orchid
lede: Light orchid is a very pale, pink-leaning purple, a tint of orchid carried in the ISCC-NBS 1955 standard as well as the 2010 xkcd survey.

sections.title: Standard and crowd agree
sections.body:
ISCC-NBS 1955 places this swatch in block 249, within the light purplish pink category, and the 2010 xkcd survey separately collected the same name for a nearly identical hue, so two independent systems converge on "light orchid" here [1]. That double sourcing is less common than it sounds: most of its names come from the xkcd survey alone [1].

The nearest named colors on file are [[pale-hortense-violet]], [[light-lavender]], [[pale-lavender]] and [[pale-violet]], at 2.8, 4.5, 4.7 and 7.5 ΔE [2].

sections.title: Field notes
sections.body: Our archive of 23,781 paintings, as photographed, holds no painting where this exact pale purple covers five percent or more of the canvas [3]. A tint this light and this saturated sits outside the range aged oil paint and varnish typically produce [3]. A match would be a computed color comparison, never a pigment identification [3].
